reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of this work lies in distinguishing between population-wide and category-specific information flows. The ILS^dl operator serves as a log-likelihood ratio that quantifies deviation from expected market behavior under the null hypothesis of no insider activity. It is computed through a four-stage pipeline: first, classifying market resolutions into binary discrete-event types; second, filtering out non-informative deadline-resolved markets; third, recovering T_event timestamps using a multi-tiered LLM cascade; fourth, computing the score based on observed price movements relative to a hazard-adjusted baseline. This process enables detection of anomalous price dynamics that may indicate early information dissemination. The hazard decay baseline corrects for natural market volatility by modeling the time-dependent risk of event realization using a Weibull distribution, which better fits empirical data than exponential decay. Anchor-robustness screening ensures that these anomalies persist across small temporal shifts, reducing false positives due to misalignment of event timing. These primitives together form a robust framework for identifying potential insider trading signals at scale.
